newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp Q1 orders up, but sales flat.
newsitem.headline: Krupp Q1 orders up, but sales flat.

text.p: Germany's Krupp steel and engineering group said on Monday that incoming orders had risen in the first quarter by 5.6 percent to 6.5 billion marks, but sales were flat at 5.5 billion.

Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp chairman Gerhard Cromme said he expected earnings to improve this year, as Krupp's steel division, newly merged with the steel operations of Thyssen AG, assumes a leading role in the global marketplace.
Cromme, in remarks published before a news conference, said economic recovery in Germany was still being led from abroad.

"Economic activity picked up slightly in the first three months of 1997, but still mainly as a result of demand from abroad," he said. "It is difficult to say whether the economy in Germany will gather pace over the next few months."
Group net profits in 1995 were 208 million marks, down from 505 million the year before. Krupp said its workforce had fallen by just over 2,000 in the three months to March 31 this year to 67,575.

Cromme said details of the steel merger with Thyssen were still under discussion. He added that the fusion, creating a business with sales of around 11 billion marks and raw steel output of 15 million tonnes, represented a major step forward for all concerned.
